Overlays and the server API

Source: vignettes/overlays-and-server.Rmd
overlays-and-server.Rmd

This vignette covers the overlay family — dialog, sheet, drawer, alert-dialog — and the server-side helpers that open them and raise toasts.

Trigger-driven vs server-driven

Every overlay accepts a trigger: a UI element that opens it on click. Give the overlay an inputId and its open state is reported as a logical input$id.

library(shiny)
library(shadshiny)

shad_dialog(
  "settings",
  trigger = shad_button("Settings", variant = "outline"),
  title = "Settings",
  shad_input("name", label = "Display name"),
  footer = shad_dialog_close_button("Done")
)

The same overlay can be opened (or closed) from the server without any trigger, using shad_dialog_open() / shad_dialog_close(). Each overlay has a matching pair — shad_sheet_open(), shad_drawer_open(), shad_alert_dialog_open(), shad_popover_open(), and so on.

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$launch, {
    shad_dialog_open("settings")
  })
  observeEvent(input$settings, {
    # TRUE when open, FALSE when dismissed
    message("settings dialog open? ", input$settings)
  })
}

Dialogs built in the server

Both forms above need the overlay to exist in the UI. When the dialog’s content depends on what just happened — the row you clicked, the file that failed — build it in the server and show it, the way shiny::showModal() works:

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$delete, {
    shad_show_dialog(shad_dialog(
      "confirm_delete",
      title = paste("Delete", input$selected_project, "?"),
      description = "This cannot be undone.",
      footer = tagList(
        shad_dialog_close_button(),
        shad_button(inputId = "confirm_delete_go", "Delete",
                    variant = "destructive")
      )
    ))
  })
}

The overlay is appended to <body>, opens itself, and — by default — destroys and removes itself once it closes. Nothing to clean up, and no ids left behind. shad_show_dialog() also takes shad_alert_dialog(), shad_sheet() and shad_drawer().

Inputs inside it are live while it is open, so input$confirm_delete_go works exactly as it would in a UI-declared dialog. They vanish with the dialog, though: read what you need in the observer, or pass transient = FALSE to keep the overlay (and its values) in the document so it can be reopened with shad_dialog_open().

shad_remove_dialog(id) closes one from the server — for a job that finished or a save that succeeded. Esc, the backdrop and shad_dialog_close_button() all still work on their own.

Confirm flows with alert-dialog

shad_alert_dialog() is the modal-confirmation pattern. Its action button is a Shiny action button with id <inputId>_confirm, so you observe the confirm the same way you observe any action button:

ui <- shad_alert_dialog(
  "wipe",
  trigger = shad_button("Delete account", variant = "destructive"),
  title = "Delete your account?",
  description = "This cannot be undone.",
  cancel = "Keep it",
  action = "Delete",
  action_variant = "destructive"
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$wipe_confirm, {
    # user pressed the destructive action
    shad_toast_success("Account deleted.")
  })
}

Toasts

Toasts are server-only notifications. shad_toast() takes a message plus title, description, variant, and duration; the shorthands shad_toast_success(), shad_toast_error(), shad_toast_warning(), and shad_toast_loading() set the variant for you.

shad_toast_success("Saved", description = "Your changes are live.")
shad_toast_error("Upload failed", description = "Check your connection.")

Loading → done

shad_toast_loading() shows an indefinite spinner and returns an id. Feed that id to shad_toast_update() when the work finishes to morph the same toast into a result — no second toast, no flicker.

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$export, {
    id <- shad_toast_loading("Exporting…")
    later::later(function() {
      shad_toast_update(id, variant = "success",
                        message = "Export ready")
    }, delay = 2)
  })
}

Dismiss programmatically with shad_toast_dismiss(id), or shad_toast_dismiss() to clear all.

Dynamic UI and modules

Components self-initialize, so overlays and inputs rendered inside renderUI() work without manual re-binding:

output$panel <- renderUI({
  shad_dialog("dyn", trigger = shad_button("Open"),
              title = "Rendered on demand", shad_p("Hello."))
})

All inputIds pass through session$ns(), so components and their update_shad_*() / shad_*_open() helpers are safe inside Shiny modules — use the same bare id in UI and server as you would with base inputs.
